questions.q: List the nine functions of media in society as per the NCERT Class 11 Home Science textbook.
questions.a: The nine functions are: 1. Information, 2. Persuasion/Motivation, 3. Entertainment, 4. Interpretation, 5. Transmission of values, 6. Education or training, 7. Coordination, 8. Behavioural change, 9. Development. A wrong answer (e.g., listing only 3-4 functions or confusing functions with types of media like "print, electronic, digital") reveals that the student has memorised isolated bullet points without understanding the comprehensive functional framework the textbook provides.

questions.q: Explain in your own words the difference between the "Information" function and the "Interpretation" function of media. Give one original example for each.
questions.a: Information function involves providing raw facts, data, or news (e.g., a news bulletin stating "Rainfall in Kerala was 30% above average this monsoon"). Interpretation function goes further by explaining the meaning, context, or implications of that information (e.g., an analytical article explaining how the excess rainfall will affect crop prices, reservoir levels, and flood risk). A wrong answer that treats them as synonyms or gives the same example for both shows the student cannot distinguish between data dissemination and sense-making — a critical analytical skill for senior secondary.

questions.q: A community radio station in a tribal area broadcasts a weekly program that includes: (a) local market prices for forest produce, (b) a dramatized story about a girl who convinces her parents to let her continue schooling, (c) a folk song about handwashing, and (d) an interview with a block development officer about a new irrigation scheme. Identify which media function each segment primarily serves.
questions.a: (a) Market prices → Information; (b) Dramatized story on girls' education → Persuasion/Motivation and Transmission of values; (c) Folk song on handwashing → Education/training and Behavioural change; (d) Interview on irrigation scheme → Information and Development. A wrong answer that assigns only one function per segment or misses the dual functions (e.g., labeling the folk song only as Entertainment) reveals the student struggles to see overlapping functions in real-world media content — a common board exam trap.

questions.q: Compare the role of traditional folk media (e.g., puppetry, folk theatre) and modern digital media (e.g., WhatsApp, YouTube) in performing the "Transmission of values" function in a rural Indian context. Analyze two strengths and two limitations of each.
questions.a: Traditional folk media strengths: culturally embedded, high trust, uses local dialect/idioms; limitations: limited reach, not easily scalable, difficult to update. Modern digital media strengths: vast reach, interactive, multimedia (audio-visual), easily shareable; limitations: digital divide (access/ literacy), risk of misinformation, lower cultural resonance. A wrong answer that simply says "traditional is old, modern is new" or focuses only on technology without linking to the specific function of values transmission shows superficial analysis lacking socio-cultural depth.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The 'Development' function of media is merely the sum of its Information, Education, and Behavioural change functions." Defend your position with reasoning.
questions.a: The claim is partially true but reductionist. Development function is indeed catalysed by information, education, and behavioural change, but it also requires Coordination (linking specialists with communities), Interpretation (making complex policies understandable), and Persuasion (motivating collective action). Development is an emergent, systemic outcome — not just a linear sum. A wrong answer that agrees without qualification or disagrees without referencing the other six functions shows inability to synthesize across the functional framework — a key competency for 4-6 mark board questions.

questions.q: Design a 3-minute media campaign plan for promoting millet consumption among urban teenagers. Specify: (a) which media (traditional/modern) you would use, (b) which three media functions you would prioritize, and (c) one measurable indicator for each chosen function.
questions.a: Example answer: (a) Instagram Reels + school-level nukkad natak (street play); (b) Prioritized functions: Entertainment (engaging reels/play), Persuasion/Motivation (influencer testimonials, peer pressure in play), Education/training (quick recipe demos, nutritional facts); (c) Indicators: Entertainment → views/shares/comments; Persuasion → pledge sign-ups; Education → quiz scores on millet nutrition. A poor answer that chooses only one medium, lists functions without justification, or gives vague indicators ("awareness") reveals inability to translate theory into actionable communication design — a higher-order skill expected in competency-based questions.
